prompt: Match each thing a person feels to the metric for it.
Why did INP replace First Input Delay?

choices.text: FID measured only the first interaction's wait
choices.why: Right. Every tap after the first could be slow and FID would not say.

choices.text: FID was measured on the server
choices.why: Both are measured in the browser.

choices.text: FID counted scrolling
choices.why: Scrolling is not an interaction for either.

choices.text: Browsers stopped supporting the API that FID was built on
choices.why: The reason was what FID measured, not an API.

prompt: Where are the three Core Web Vitals measured?

choices.text: On the server, from its logs
choices.why: A server cannot see a paint or a shift.

choices.text: In the build, from the size of the bundle
choices.why: Size is a cause; the metrics measure what a person lives through.

choices.text: In the browser
choices.why: Yes, by its own performance APIs, while the page is used.

choices.text: At the CDN
choices.why: A CDN sees requests, not paints.

prompt: A page paints its header at 200 ms and its article at 3 s. What is its LCP?

choices.text: 200 ms
choices.why: That is when something was painted, not the largest thing.

choices.text: 3 s
choices.why: Right. The article is the largest content.

choices.text: The average of the two, 1.6 s
choices.why: LCP is one moment, not an average.

choices.text: 3.2 s, the sum of both paints
choices.why: Nothing is added up.

prompt: When does the LCP candidate stop changing?

choices.text: When the load event fires
choices.why: Content painted after load still counts until the person acts.

choices.text: After 2.5 seconds
choices.why: That is a threshold, not a deadline.

choices.text: When the last image of the page finishes downloading
choices.why: The last image is not necessarily the largest.

choices.text: At the first interaction, or when hidden
choices.why: Yes. After that the page is the person's.

prompt: Which of these can be an LCP element? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A block of text
choices.why: Yes, as the planner's notice was.

choices.text: An image drawn as a CSS background
choices.why: Yes, it counts as an image.

choices.text: The poster of a video
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: An image below the window, not yet scrolled to
choices.why: Only what is inside the window counts.

choices.text: An empty box with a large background colour
choices.why: A colour is not content.

prompt: Match each part of an LCP to its usual fix.

pairs.right: A faster or closer server, or a cache
Let the browser find the image in the HTML

prompt: Which of these is an interaction for INP?

choices.text: A key press
choices.why: Yes, as are a click and a tap.

choices.text: Scrolling the page
choices.why: Scrolling is not counted.

choices.text: Hovering over a link
choices.why: Hovering is not counted.

choices.text: The page finishing its load
choices.why: Nobody did anything.

prompt: A button turns grey at once, then loads data for a second. Why is its INP short?

choices.text: Loading data is not counted by any metric
choices.why: It is just not what INP measures.

choices.text: Grey buttons are excused
choices.why: Nothing about colour is excused.

choices.text: The next paint came at once
choices.why: Right. INP ends at the first frame after the tap.

choices.text: Because the data arrived over the network rather than from the page
choices.why: Where the data comes from plays no part.

prompt: Put the three parts of one interaction in the order they happen.
On a page with many interactions, which one sets the INP?

choices.text: The first
choices.why: That is what FID used to look at.

choices.text: The slowest, ignoring one in every fifty
choices.why: Yes. One freak delay on a long visit does not decide it.

choices.text: The average of all of them
choices.why: An average would hide the slow ones.

choices.text: The last
choices.why: Order plays no part.

prompt: Why is the same shift scored higher on a small screen?

choices.text: Phones are judged more strictly
choices.why: The thresholds are the same; the fractions are not.

choices.text: Phones repaint more often
choices.why: Repaints are not scored.

choices.text: Touch screens count every scroll as a shift
choices.why: Scrolling is not a layout shift.

choices.text: It covers a bigger fraction of the window
choices.why: Right, and its distance is a larger part of it too.

prompt: A person taps a menu and it opens, pushing text down. Does that count towards CLS?

choices.text: No, it came within half a second of the tap
choices.why: Yes. The person asked for that movement.

choices.text: Yes, every shift counts
choices.why: A shift the person caused is excused.

choices.text: Only on a phone
choices.why: The rule is the same on every screen.

choices.text: Only when the menu is an image
choices.why: What moved plays no part.

prompt: Content covering half the window moves down a tenth of it. About what does that shift score?
A page has one burst of shifts as it loads, then stays open for an hour without moving. What is its CLS?

choices.text: That burst, divided by the hour
choices.why: Nothing is divided by time.

choices.text: Zero, because the last minutes were still
choices.why: The burst still happened.

choices.text: The score of that one burst
choices.why: Right. CLS is the worst window, however long the page stays open.

choices.text: Every shift ever made on it, summed
choices.why: The score is the worst window, not a total.

prompt: Match each metric to its threshold for good.
When does a page pass a Core Web Vital?

choices.text: When its median visit is good
choices.why: The median would let half the visitors have a bad time.

choices.text: When three quarters of visits are good
choices.why: Yes: the 75th percentile, per metric and per kind of device.

choices.text: When your own measurement says good
choices.why: One measurement is one visit.

choices.text: When every visit is good
choices.why: The slowest visits are often a network no page could help.

prompt: A page scores good on all three metrics. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It is fast in every way that matters
choices.why: It says nothing of a search or a full navigation.

choices.text: It works offline
choices.why: No metric here measures that.

choices.text: It will rank first in search results
choices.why: The lesson makes no such claim.

choices.text: It is not slow in those three ways
choices.why: Right. Other goals are the team's to set and measure.

prompt: Why is web-vitals installed as a dependency of the app and not as a tool?

choices.text: It runs in every visitor's browser
choices.why: Yes. It ships with the page.

choices.text: npm refuses to install it as a development dependency
choices.why: npm would install it either way.

choices.text: Tools cannot be pinned
choices.why: Every tool here is pinned.

choices.text: Only Vite can read it
choices.why: Vite bundles it; that is not the reason.

prompt: What does the attribution build add to each value?

choices.text: A rating from Google's servers
choices.why: The rating is computed in the page.

choices.text: A screenshot
choices.why: It sends no image.

choices.text: The element or interaction that caused it
choices.why: Right, and for INP its three parts.

choices.text: The visitor's address
choices.why: It knows nothing of the visitor.

prompt: Why does main.ts set the notice with textContent and not innerHTML?

choices.text: textContent is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given.

choices.text: The text must not be read as HTML
choices.why: Yes. It is text from a server.

choices.text: innerHTML would cause a layout shift
choices.why: Either one moves the page the same way.

choices.text: innerHTML does not work on a paragraph
choices.why: It works on any element.

prompt: On the slowed phone, why was #notice also the LCP element?

choices.text: It has a background colour
choices.why: A colour is not content.

choices.text: web-vitals always picks the first paragraph of the page
choices.why: It picks the largest.

choices.text: It was the element that shifted
choices.why: #app shifted; the notice pushed it.

choices.text: It was the largest text on the page
choices.why: Right. Two lines on a narrow screen, arriving last.

prompt: With the notice sent by the server, what LCP did the slowed phone measure, in milliseconds?
Keeping room for the notice made CLS zero. Why did LCP barely move?

choices.text: The text was still fetched by the script
choices.why: Yes. The room was there; the words still came last.

choices.text: min-height delays painting
choices.why: It only reserves room.

choices.text: LCP and CLS are the same measurement
choices.why: They moved apart in this very step.

choices.text: The server was slowed by the change to the stylesheet
choices.why: The server serves the same file just as fast.

prompt: The first slow click spent 1762 of 1888 ms processing. What was the cause?

choices.text: The input delay of the tap
choices.why: It was one millisecond.

choices.text: Fetching courses.json again
choices.why: The plan was already in the page.

choices.text: Counting by filtering all sessions per course
choices.why: Right. Twenty-five million comparisons in one task.

choices.text: The slow network
choices.why: This run slowed the processor, not the network.

prompt: After counting once, 723 ms of processing were left. What was it doing?

choices.text: Counting again
choices.why: The count is one pass now.

choices.text: Building five thousand list items
choices.why: Yes, which is why drawing a hundred fixed it.

choices.text: Waiting for the network
choices.why: Processing is the handler running.

choices.text: Running web-vitals
choices.why: It costs almost nothing.

prompt: Some work cannot be removed. How does a handler keep its INP short anyway?

choices.text: Run the work before the click
choices.why: The work depends on the click.

choices.text: Hide the page until the work is done
choices.why: The person would see nothing happen, for longer.

choices.text: Run it in an async function, which never blocks the main thread
choices.why: An async function still runs on the main thread between its awaits.

choices.text: Show the click landed, then yield and work
choices.why: Right, with setTimeout or scheduler.yield().

prompt: Why does the planner send its values with sendBeacon and not fetch?

choices.text: The request outlives the page
choices.why: Yes. The values are final only when the page is left.

choices.text: fetch cannot send JSON
choices.why: It can.

choices.text: sendBeacon compresses the data before sending it
choices.why: Compression is not the reason.

choices.text: The server only accepts beacons
choices.why: It accepts any POST.

prompt: The log got LCP and CLS but no INP. Why?

choices.text: sendBeacon dropped it
choices.why: Nothing was sent to drop.

choices.text: INP needs a phone
choices.why: It is measured on any device.

choices.text: The click was quicker than 40 ms
choices.why: Right. Quicker interactions are not reported.

choices.text: The server rejected the INP line because it arrived after the others
choices.why: The server writes whatever it receives.
